Really thrilling game, with some truly difficult timed moments, the peak of which happens maybe 1/2 way through. (RIP a few times Agent *Name Redacted*, before I was able to learn how to properly diffuse a bomb. Sorry, at least I figured it out eventually...) But besides that, it's basically one of my favorite techy game mystery interfaces: poking around in computers and researching (snooping) on different people via high powered invasive search engine. You really feel like you're in on the action. I think the ending is a bit unfortunate, but only in that a number of rather....intense things happened....and I'm about to look up if there are alternate endings, or if this is just a linear pathway it leads you to. Overall, I thoroughly recommend. Creates a cool world, does the fun thing of dropping you, the newbie, into a new job and has just enough tutorial-lite info to get you off and running. If you like any sort of detective/unfolding mystery game, it's perfect! I could see this expanding into so many other cases and worlds, or having repeat instances with some key, returning characters. Speaking of characters, I really liked a lot of the other detectives, and our mysterious hacker friend. Great voice acting, lost of personality.

I grade The Operator A-. This is an excellent investigation game with a great premise and fantastic presentation, including the music. While it doesn't have Hollywood-style hacking, given that its setting is in 1992 and you're working in a government alphabet agency, the developers nailed the look and feel of a stripped down government UI. Even right down to a part where you use an even [i]older[/i] computer and the visual area changes from 16:9 to 4:3. Nice touch.

The story is very well written. I didn't detect a single typo or weird turn of phrase. A lot of detective games here on Steam are made by non-English developers, and so they tend to get wonky in localization. The Operator does not have that issue. The story is almost entirely logical and internally consistent, and it was fun to experience.

The only thing is the story's wheels fell off at the very end. While the story beats and twists were a bit obvious, the final hard twist -- though it was presented really well -- makes absolutely no logical sense even within the context of the world that is presented to us. I come away from it with a lot more questions, but not the good "What are they going to do next?" kind. It's more the "Why did the basic premise happen in the first place?" kind. Unless there was some subtlety I missed, I can think of a thousand reasons why the first step of the plot shouldn't have happened, and that sort of makes the ending a little bit of a letdown.

But don't let that dissuade you. I'm happy to have bought the game and supported the developer, especially because the gameplay was excellent. I really enjoyed the act of investigating as a government agent and having tools like face-scanning and an omni-database just a mouse click away. Don't get me wrong, I enjoy games with hacking -- whether Hollwood hacking like Orwell or more script-based hacking like HackNet -- but it was really fun to be an agent for the "other side" and just have some improbable tools at my fingertips. If there is a sequel, while I hope the writing makes a little more logical sense, I really encourage the devs to keep the gameplay just as it is.

[spoiler] Everybody dies. Well, okay, one person is on the run from the law and another is imprisoned for life, but everybody else dies with extra fluff added to the details of what happened to twist the knife even harder that, after everything you did throughout the game, it was all meaningless because you failed. Might as well have had Patrick Star read me the extended cut of the Ugly Barnacle.[/spoiler]

The intensity of the tragic ending was so dramatic, I went online so I could see what I did to get the bad ending because it gave me such bad whiplash. Nope, no bad ending. Just one ending. It didn't earn or build up to leaving me holding an empty bag of misery. It has extra secrets, but because its ending left me feeling the way it did, I don't feel like I have any reason to TRY and learn more. It doesn't feel like there's a point to learning more outside of satisfying the curiosity I was feeling right up until the game kicked me in the crotch.

If you don't mind stories that abruptly end tragically, literally everything else about the game felt solid. I almost want to give this a recommendation. However, with the ending leaving me feel like nothing was accomplished but a few hours burned down the hole, I feel like I can only recommend this with "Play it at your own risk."

The Operator is a very short (3 to 4 hours at best) interactive visual novel with good production value. The interface looks clean and easy to use, the voice acting is good, and the interactive elements are pretty decent. For a visual novel. 

It is presented, however, as a game of deduction and puzzle solving. The puzzles and deductions are shallow with too much handholding. As you progress new mechanics are introduced, and then discarded immediately after. This gives the mistaken impression that much more content is waiting for you and puzzles will get more difficult. And then the game is over.

The story is equally shallow. The opening scene reveals too much, making the big reveal at the end something you can piece together within a few minutes of playing the game. The ending is a cliffhanger of sorts, but it makes this game feel like the opening chapter of a larger story that has not been written. Worse is that none of the conspiracy is ever explained, leaving you with many questions that are unlikely to be answered. There are no divergent paths, only one ending, and zero replay value.

If you go into this game expecting a visual novel, you will have an entertaining few hours with an okay story and underwhelming finale. If you go into this game expecting deduction, investigation, and puzzle solving, you will find only disappointment. This ultimately leads to my negative review. For a visual novel it is too short with an unresolved story, and for an investigation game the puzzles are too simple. The Operator has a lot of unmet potential, which is a shame.
